root.label: Partial ordering
root.note: How the compiler picks the most specialized template when conversions tie.

children.label: Place in overload resolution
children.note: A tie-breaker that runs only after conversion sequences fail to separate candidates.

children.label: Conversions first
children.note: f('a') picks a template with T = char over f(int), which needs a promotion.

children.label: Non-template wins ties
children.note: With equal conversions a non-template beats any template specialization.

children.label: Tie-breaker order
children.note: Non-template, then more specialized, then more constrained, then non-rewritten, then non-reversed.

children.label: The procedure
children.note: Synthesize unique types for one template and deduce the other from it, both ways.

children.label: Types considered
children.note: In a call, only parameters with explicit arguments; default arguments are ignored.

children.label: Adjustments
children.note: References and then top-level cv are stripped before deducing.

children.label: More specialized
children.note: Deduction succeeds one way for all types and fails the other way for some.

children.label: Ambiguity
children.note: g(T, int*) and g(int*, T) each win one position, so g(p, p) is ambiguous.

children.label: References and packs
children.note: Extra tie-breaks when deduction succeeds in both directions.

children.label: Lvalue beats rvalue
children.note: f(T&) is more specialized than f(T&&) for an lvalue argument.

children.label: More cv wins
children.note: const T& beats T&& for a const lvalue, after both bind const int&.

children.label: Forwarding wins conversions
children.note: For a non-const lvalue T&& binds int&, which beats const int& before ordering runs.

children.label: Trailing pack loses
children.note: On a tie, f(T) beats f(T, Ts...) because of the empty pack (CWG 1395).

children.label: Constraints
children.note: C++20 lets the more constrained template win, under conditions.

children.label: Same shape required
children.note: Only templates with equivalent template parameters and parameter types are compared by constraints.

children.label: Concepts subsume
children.note: Repeated requires is_integral_v<T> clauses are different atomic constraints and never subsume.

children.label: Non-template members
children.note: Constraints also order non-template members of class templates with equal parameters.

children.label: Specializations
children.note: Explicit and partial specializations use the same ordering differently.

children.label: Explicit ones never compete
children.note: They attach to the primary template chosen where they are declared.

children.label: Class partial ordering
children.note: Each partial specialization is rewritten as a function template taking S<args>.

children.label: Ambiguous use ill-formed
children.note: S<T, int> and S<int, T> both match S<int, int>, so that use is an error.

children.label: Must beat primary
children.note: A partial specialization must be more specialized than the primary template.

children.label: Rewritten operators
children.note: C++20 adds reversed and rewritten comparison candidates.

children.label: Reversed parameter order
children.note: A reversed template candidate is ordered with its parameters reversed.

children.label: Late tie-breaker
children.note: A reversed non-template still beats a non-reversed template.

children.label: Non-const member ==
children.note: Ambiguous by the letter of C++20; GCC and Clang accept it with a warning.
